section.content: Quantization techniques are described with respect to an Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) model in wireless communications. The device performs quantization with respect to the AI/ML model. The device then performs wireless communication by using the AI/ML model.
描述了关于无线通信中人工智能(AI)/机器学习(ML)模型的量化技术。设备执行关于AI/ML模型的量化。然后，该设备通过利用AI/ML模型执行无线通信。

Quantization of artificial intelligence AI/machine learning ML modelsCross Reference to Related Applications

The present disclosure is part of a non-provisional application requiring the benefit of priority from U.S. patent application Ser. No. 63/485,557 filed on day 2022, month 2, and 17, the contents of which are incorporated herein by reference in their entirety.

Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to wireless communications, and more particularly to quantization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models in wireless communications.

Background

Unless otherwise indicated herein, the approaches described in this section are not admitted to be prior art to the following claims and are not admitted to be prior art by inclusion in this section.

In communication systems, such as wireless communication according to the third generation partnership project (3 GPP) standard, many functions on the User Equipment (UE) side often have one corresponding function on the network side and vice versa. In the context of AI/ML, this may be referred to as a bilateral AI/ML model, also referred to as a self-encoder. However, since the real world is composed of a simulated and continuous spatio-temporal environment, training of the AI/ML model may require and/or result in a tremendous amount of data, including potential vectors and gradient vectors, and the like. Without proper processing, such huge amounts of data would place an excessive burden on the UE side and the network side, even overwhelmingly. Therefore, a solution is needed for quantifying data of an AI/ML model in wireless communication.

Disclosure of Invention

The following summary is provided for purposes of illustration only and is not intended to be limiting in any way. That is, the following summary is intended to introduce a selection of concepts, benefits, and advantages of the novel and non-obvious techniques described herein. Selected embodiments will be further described in the detailed description. Accordingly, the following summary is not intended to identify essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used to determine the scope of the claimed subject matter.

The objective of the present disclosure is to propose a solution or a solution to solve the problems described herein. More particularly, various aspects presented in this disclosure relate to quantization of AI/ML models in wireless communications. It is believed that the implementation of various proposed solutions can solve or alleviate the above-mentioned problems. The various schemes presented herein may be used in a variety of applications and scenarios, such as, but not limited to, channel State Information (CSI) compression, denoising (or noise reduction), quantization, encoding, error correction code, modulation, peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction, and image compression.

In an aspect, a method may involve performing quantization with respect to an AI/ML model. The method may also involve performing wireless communication by utilizing an AI/ML model.

In another aspect, an apparatus may include a transceiver configured for wireless communication and a processor coupled to the transceiver. The processor may perform quantization with respect to the AI/ML model. The processor may also perform wireless communication by utilizing an AI/ML model.

Notably, while the description provided herein may be in the context of certain radio access technologies, networks, and wireless communication network topologies, such as fifth generation (5G)/new wireless (NR) mobile communications, the proposed concepts, schemes, and any variants/derivatives thereof may be implemented in, for, and through other types of radio access technologies, networks, and network topologies, such as, but not limited to, evolved Packet System (EPS), long Term Evolution (LTE), LTE-Advanced Pro, internet of things (IoT), narrowband internet of things (NB-IoT), industrial internet of things (IIoT), internet of vehicles (V2X), and non-terrestrial network (NTN) communications. Accordingly, the scope of the disclosure is not limited to the examples described herein.

Detailed Description

Detailed embodiments and implementations of the claimed subject matter are disclosed in this specification. It is to be understood, however, that the disclosed embodiments and implementations are merely illustrative of the claimed subject matter, which may be embodied in various forms. This description may, however, be embodied in many different forms and should not be construed as limited to the exemplary embodiments and implementations set forth herein. Rather, these exemplary embodiments and implementations are intended to fully complete the description of the present specification and to fully convey the scope of the present specification to those skilled in the art. In the following description, details of well-known features and techniques may be omitted to avoid unnecessarily obscuring the presented embodiments and implementations.

SUMMARY

Implementations consistent with the present specification relate to various techniques, methods, schemes, and/or solutions related to quantization of AI/ML models in wireless communications. Many of the possible solutions can be implemented individually or in combination according to the present description. That is, although these possible solutions may be described separately below, two or more of these possible solutions may be implemented in one or another combination.

FIG. 1 illustrates an example network environment 100 in which various solutions and schemes according to the present description may be implemented. Fig. 2-12 illustrate examples of implementations of various proposed schemes in a network environment 100 according to the present description. The following description of various proposed schemes is provided with reference to fig. 1-12.

Referring to fig. 1, a network environment 100 may involve a user equipment UE 110 in wireless communication with a radio access network RAN 120 (e.g., a 5G NR mobile network or other type of network, such as a non-terrestrial network NTN). UE 110 may communicate wirelessly with RAN 120 via a terrestrial network node 125 (e.g., a base station, eNB, gNB, or transmission and reception point TRP) or a non-terrestrial network node 128 (e.g., a satellite), and UE 110 may be located within the coverage of one cell 135 associated with terrestrial network node 125 and/or non-terrestrial network node 128. RAN 120 may be part of network 130. In network environment 100, UE 110 and network 130 (via terrestrial network node 125 and/or non-terrestrial network node 128) may implement various schemes related to quantization of AI/ML models in wireless communications, as described below. In this specification, the bilateral AI/ML model may be being trained for CSI compression, noise reduction, quantization, encoding, error correction code, modulation, PAPR reduction, and/or image compression. It is noted that although various proposal schemes, options and methods may be described below separately, in practical applications, these proposal schemes, options and methods may be implemented separately or in combination. That is, in some cases, one or more of the proposal, option, and method may be implemented separately or separately. In other cases, some or all of the proposal schemes, options, and methods may be implemented in combination.

According to various proposals of the present description, continuous space may be discretized into a limited number of representative points. Furthermore, each representative point may be indexed with a limited number of bits. Under the proposed scheme, quantization in the latent space may compress representations of one or more latent vectors in forward pass of the training phase and the reasoning phase of the AI/ML model. Furthermore, quantization in the gradient space may compress representations of one or more gradient vectors in the back propagation of the training phase of the AI/ML model. Furthermore, quantization in the data space may help facilitate the data collection process by compressing the samples, thereby reducing its overhead.

Fig. 2 illustrates an example scenario 200 of a quantization framework in potential space according to the proposed solution of the present specification. Under the proposed scheme, quantization in potential space may be bilateral and may involve a quantization side and a dequantization side. Notably, although the example illustrated in fig. 2 relates to CSI compression, the proposed scheme may also be used for other applications (e.g., noise reduction, quantization, encoding, error correction code, modulation, PAPR reduction, and/or image compression). Under the proposed scheme, the quantization side may involve two steps, namely a first step (step 1) and a second step (step 2). In step 1, the CSI generation portion of the AI/ML model can construct a potential vector. In step 2, one or more quantizer modules may convert the continuous potential vector into a limited number of bitstreams. Under the proposed scheme, the dequantization side may also involve two steps, namely a first step (step 1) and a second step (step 2). In step 1, the dequantizer may recover the potential vector from the bitstream. In step 2, the CSI reconstruction portion of the AI/ML model may recover CSI from the potential vectors.

Fig. 3 illustrates an example scenario 300 of quantifying training perceptions in potential space according to the proposed solution of the present specification. Under the proposed scheme, quantization may be either training perceptual or training non-perceptual. Part (a) of fig. 3 illustrates an example of training non-perceptual (TNA) quantization under a proposed scheme, and part (B) of fig. 3 illustrates an example of training perceptual (TA) quantization under a proposed scheme. Under TNA quantization, the AI/ML model may be exposed to the quantization method only in Forward Pass (FP) of the inference phase. Under TA quantization, the AI/ML model may only be exposed to the quantization method during the inference phase. This is because quantization is not trivial during the training phase and Back Propagation (BP) is not possible.

Fig. 4 illustrates an example scenario 400 of training perception quantized in potential space under the scheme described in this disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, the quantized training perceptions in back propagation can be enhanced by one or more methods. The first approach may involve approximating the quantization function with a micro-functionable function, as shown in part (a) of fig. 4. Thus, in view of the scalability of the quantization function, back propagation can be ensured. The second approach may involve approximating the gradient of the quantization function, as shown in part (B) of fig. 4. Thus, back propagation may only be approximated at non-minuscule points. A third method may involve quantized artificial gradients, as shown in part (C) of fig. 4. For example, the gradient of the quantization function may be replaced by a constant over its entire domain.

According to the schemes described in this disclosure, the learning about quantization in potential space may mean whether quantization parameters and/or configurations may change during the training phase. Thus, learning is a unique feature of training perceptual quantization methods. Examples of quantization learnability may include a learnable clipper, a learnable transformation of quantized input/output (I/O), a learnable quantization level, and a learnable quantization interval. The learnable quantization may present adjustable configurations and parameters during the training phase. Examples of quantization non-learning (NL) may include a fixed uniform quantization that remains unchanged at training phase intervals and levels.

Fig. 5 illustrates an example scenario 500 of codeword allocation quantized in potential space under the scheme described in the present disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, the mapping of codeword allocations may involve one or more of Scalar Quantization (SQ), vector Quantization (VQ), and segment vector quantization. Part (a) of fig. 5 shows one example of SQ, part (B) of fig. 5 shows one example of VQ, and part (C) of fig. 5 shows one example of segment vector quantization. Under the proposed scheme, SQ may involve mapping one element on a potential vector to a new discretized element one by one. Furthermore, VQ may involve mapping the potential vector to a new discretized vector. Furthermore, segment vector quantization may involve decomposing the potential vector into a plurality of segments, each segment undergoing VQ.

Fig. 6 illustrates an example scenario 600 of vector quantized segmentation in potential space under the scheme described in this disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, segmentation may occur before VQ. The reason for the segmentation before VQ is that the codebook design of VQ is computationally expensive and its complexity tends to increase as the dimension of the input increases. Thus, segmentation helps reduce dimensionality. Furthermore, the number of CSI samples in the training data set may exceed the number of representative points and may be too large if there are no segments. Thus, segmentation may alleviate excessive demand for training data. Referring to fig. 6, in the segmented VQ framework under the proposed scheme, training potential points may be broken down into smaller segments, each of which designs a corresponding VQ codebook. The same segmentation may be applied during the inference phase and a corresponding codebook may be assigned to each segment during the inference phase. In the inference phase, codewords of all segments may be concatenated into one final codeword, and the final codeword may be mapped into a bitstream.

Fig. 7 illustrates an example scenario 700 regarding quantized reasoning in potential space under the scheme described in the present disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, reasoning with the potentially quantized bilateral AI/ML model may involve multiple steps, as shown in fig. 7. In a first step (step 1), the input may be measured and input to an encoder. In a second step (step 2), the output of the encoder may produce an original potential. In a third step (step 3), the potential may be quantized and a codeword generated and sent to the decoder. In a fourth step (step 4), the codeword may be dequantized. In a fifth step (step 5), the dequantized codeword may be input to a decoder and a desired output is generated.

Fig. 8 illustrates an example scenario 800 of classification of quantization methods under the aspects of the present disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, the quantization method can be classified according to training perceptions, learning properties, and mappings (or codeword allocations), as shown in fig. 8. Such classification may provide a comprehensive description of any quantization method.

Fig. 9 illustrates an example scenario 900 of quantization in gradient space under the teachings of the present disclosure. Under the proposed scheme, gradients may also be exchanged if the back propagation loops through two entities (e.g., UE and gNB). Gradients may impose a large overhead on the communication infrastructure and should therefore be quantified. Under the proposed scheme, gradient quantization may be required for back propagation, which is not necessarily the same as the potential quantizer. In the example shown in fig. 9, even gradient quantization is bilateral quantization for CSI compression.

Fig. 10 illustrates an example scenario 1000 of quantization in data collection under the aspects of the present disclosure. The data collection may include collecting data by the UE and/or the network (e.g., the gNB) and sending the collected data to the other side. Each sample may be accompanied by various ancillary information and may accumulate over time. Thus, the overhead generated may be excessive. Under the proposed scheme, quantization can also be implemented in the data collection phase, as shown in fig. 10.

Example implementation

Fig. 11 illustrates an example communication system 1100 that includes at least one example device 1110 and one example device 1120, in accordance with embodiments of the present disclosure. Devices 1110 and 1120 may perform various functions to implement the schemes, techniques, processes, and methods described herein with respect to CSI compression and decompression, including the various schemes described above with respect to various proposed designs, concepts, schemes, systems, and methods, including network environment 100, and the processes described below. Devices 1110 and 1120 may be part of an electronic device that may be a network device or UE (e.g., UE 110), such as a portable or mobile device, a wearable device, an in-vehicle device or vehicle, a wireless communication device, or a computing device. For example, device 1110 and device 1120 may be implemented in a smart phone, a smart watch, a personal digital assistant, an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) in a vehicle, a digital camera, or a computing device such as a tablet, notebook, or notebook computer. Devices 1110 and 1120 may also be part of machine type devices, which may be IoT devices such as fixed or stationary devices, home devices, roadside units (RSUs), wired communication devices, or computing devices. For example, device 1110 and device 1120 may be implemented in a smart thermostat, a smart refrigerator, a smart door lock, a wireless audio box, or a home control center. In the various aspects described above, device 1110 and device 1120 may be implemented in or as network devices or UEs. Devices 1110 and 1120 may include at least some of the components shown in fig. 11, such as processor 1112 and processor 1122. Devices 1110 and 1120 may also include one or more other components (e.g., internal power supplies, display devices, and/or user interface devices) that are not relevant to the proposed solution of the present disclosure, and thus, for simplicity and brevity, these components of devices 1110 and 1120 are neither shown in fig. 11 nor described below.

That is, although the singular term "processor" is used herein to refer to the processors 1112 and 1122, in some embodiments, the processors 1112 and 1122 may include multiple processors, while in other embodiments they may be a single processor, in accordance with the present disclosure. In another aspect, the processors 1112 and 1122 may be implemented in hardware (and optionally firmware) with electronic components including, but not limited to, one or more transistors, one or more diodes, one or more capacitors, one or more resistors, one or more inductors, one or more memristors, and/or one or more varactors, configured and arranged to achieve the particular objects of the present disclosure. In other words, in at least some embodiments, the processors 1112 and 1122 are special purpose machines specifically designed, arranged, and configured to perform specific tasks, including those involving AI/ML model quantization in wireless communications, in accordance with various embodiments of the present disclosure.

In some embodiments, transceiver 1116 may communicate wirelessly with different types of wireless networks, with different Radio Access Technologies (RATs). That is, the transceiver 1126 may be equipped with multiple transmit antennas and multiple receive antennas for MIMO wireless communication

In some implementations, the device 1110 may further include a memory 1114 coupled to the processor 1112, the memory capable of being accessed by the processor 1112 and storing data. In some implementations, the device 1120 may further include a memory 1124 coupled to the processor 1122, the memory being capable of being accessed by the processor 1122 and storing data. Each of memory 1114 and memory 1124 can include a Random Access Memory (RAM), such as Dynamic RAM (DRAM), static RAM (SRAM), thyristor RAM (T-RAM), and/or zero capacitance RAM (Z-RAM). Example procedure

Fig. 12 illustrates an example process 1200 according to one implementation of the disclosure. Process 1200 may represent an aspect, whether partial or complete, including those relevant to the above description, of various proposed designs, concepts, schemes, systems, and methods implementing the quantization of AI/ML models in wireless communications described above. Process 1200 may include one or more operations, acts, or functions, as illustrated by one or more blocks. Although shown as discrete blocks, the individual blocks of each process may be divided into additional blocks, combined into fewer blocks, or eliminated, depending on the desired implementation. Furthermore, the blocks/sub-blocks of each process may be performed in the order shown in each figure, or alternatively, in a different order. Further, one or more blocks/sub-blocks of each process may be performed iteratively. Process 1200 may be implemented by or in device 1110 and/or device 1120, and any variations thereof. For purposes of illustration only and not by way of limitation, each process is described below in the context of device 1110 as a user device (e.g., user device 110) and device 1120 as a communication entity (e.g., a network node or base station, such as terrestrial network node 120). Process 1200 may begin at block 1210.

At 1210, process 1200 may involve processor 1112 of device 1110 (e.g., as user device 110) performing quantization with respect to AI/ML models (e.g., alone or with device 1120 as a terrestrial network node 125 or a non-terrestrial network node 128). Process 1200 may proceed from 1210 to 1220.

At 1220, the process 1200 may involve the processor 1112 performing wireless communications with the AI/ML model via the transceiver 1116.

In some implementations, in performing quantization, the process 1200 may involve the processor 1112 performing one or more of (i) quantization in a potential space, (ii) quantization in a gradient space, and (iii) quantization in a data space.

In some implementations, quantization in potential space may involve compressing representations of one or more potential vectors in forward pass of training and reasoning phases.

In some implementations, quantization in the potential space may involve one quantization stage and one dequantization stage.

In some implementations, the quantization phase may involve (i) the generation portion of the AI/ML model building a potential vector of parameters, and (ii) the quantization module converting the potential vector into a limited number of bits of the bit stream. Furthermore, the dequantization stage may involve (i) the dequantizer recovering potential vectors from the bitstream, and (ii) the reconstructed portion of the AI/ML model recovering the parameters.

In some implementations, quantization in potential space may involve a training non-perceptual TNA quantization in which the AI/ML model is exposed to quantization in a forward pass FP of the inference phase.

In some implementations, quantization in the potential space may involve a training perceptual TA quantization, where the AI/ML model is exposed to quantization during the inference phase.

In some implementations, TA quantization may involve enhancing the training perception of quantization in counter-propagating BP by performing one or more of (a) approximating the quantization function with a micro-functionable, (b) approximating the gradient of the quantization function so that BP is approximated at non-micro-points, and (c) artificially quantizing the gradient of the quantization function over the entire domain by replacing it with a constant.

In some implementations, TA quantization may involve a learnable quantization or a non-learnable quantization. In some implementations, the learnable quantization may suggest configurations or parameters that are adjusted during the training phase. Furthermore, the non-learnable quantization may involve a fixed uniform quantization with intervals and levels that remain unchanged during the training phase.

In some implementations, quantization in the potential space may involve Scalar Quantization (SQ), where one element of the potential vector is mapped to a new discretized element. Alternatively or in addition, quantization in the potential space may involve Vector Quantization (VQ), wherein the potential vector is mapped to a new discretized vector. Alternatively or in addition, quantization in the potential space may involve piecewise vector quantization, wherein the potential vector is decomposed into a plurality of segments, each segment being Vector Quantized (VQ).

In some implementations, quantization in this potential space may involve piecewise vector quantization. In some implementations, the segmented vector quantization may involve (a) decomposing one or more training potential vectors into a plurality of segments, each segment corresponding to a respective Vector Quantization (VQ) codebook, (b) applying the same segments in an inference phase, (c) assigning a respective codeword to each of the plurality of segments in the inference phase to produce a plurality of codewords, (d) concatenating the codewords of the plurality of segments in the inference phase to provide a final codeword, and (e) mapping the final codeword into a bitstream.

In some implementations, the quantification in the potential space may involve reasoning about an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model, which is a bilateral AI/ML model with potential quantification. In some implementations, reasoning about the bilateral AI/ML model with potential quantization may involve (a) measuring the input, (b) providing the result of the measurement to the output original potential encoder, (c) applying quantization to the original potential, (d) generating a codeword;

Dequantizing the codeword to produce a dequantized codeword, and (e) providing the dequantized codeword to a decoder to produce an output.

In some implementations, quantization in the gradient space may involve compressing a representation of one or more gradient vectors in the back-propagation of the training phase.

In some implementations, quantization in the data space may involve compressing samples by quantizing the data set to facilitate data collection at a lower overhead.
